citations.quote: The issue of whether a single family office is required to be licensed under the Ordinance is determined by reference to three key factors, all of which must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation: firstly, the services provided by the family office constitute one or more regulated activity as defined under the Ordinance; secondly, the family office is carrying on a business in the provision of such services; and thirdly, the business is carried on in Hong Kong.

A genuine single family office arrangement, established to serve the investment needs of members of a single family, which is not being run as a business (i.e. not receiving any income, other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family) or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective, should not in the ordinary course be considered as carrying on a business from a licensing perspective.
The sharing of office premises and administrative infrastructure by two or more family offices would not of itself automatically trigger a licensing obligation for such single family offices.

Multi-family offices are typically established and run as commercial ventures.  The issue of whether a multi-family office is required to be licensed under the Ordinance will be primarily determined by the three key factors set out in the response to Q3.

hypothesis.1de2eb561c800155c17e3c6d.distinction: Considered alternatives are: a cumulative three-factor antecedent; a reading of “must” as stating necessary conditions without establishing their legal sufficiency; and a contextual reading treating the later single-family discussion as a qualification. The first two yield the same requested antecedent, while the third is already retained in the supplied business fact. An alternative disjunction conflicts with “all” and the enumerating “and”; treating shared premises or commercial family-office status as an independent trigger conflicts with the surrounding qualifications. Consequently, only one distinct Boolean reading is defensible for this selected control. The source does not settle every upstream classification or establish a complete licensing verdict.

concerns.question: The supplied business-classification fact cannot separately express rival negation attachments in the later phrase “which is not being run as a business (i.e. not receiving any income, other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family) or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective”. Those upstream distinctions, including the ordinary-course qualification, remain unresolved within that judgment fact; this conjunction does not settle them.

The three Boolean facts express satisfaction of the enumerated antecedent, but cannot distinguish necessary conditions for a licensing obligation from legally sufficient conditions under the full Ordinance and missing authorities.

The wording “not being run as a business ... or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective” leaves uncertainty about whether negation extends to pursuit of profit. The supplied business fact preserves this upstream uncertainty but cannot separately encode the rival attachments, reimbursement conditions, or genuine single-family status.

The modalities “should not in the ordinary course”, “may be regarded”, and “increases the likelihood” cannot be represented as defeasible or probabilistic rules using these three Boolean facts. They must inform upstream judgments rather than become automatic exemptions or triggers.

The three facts express satisfaction of the selected antecedent, not whether its satisfaction is legally sufficient for an obligation under missing authorities. They also cannot establish licence possession or compliance.
